strengths: Novel mesh tokenization approach that reduces redundant vertex information by ~50% compared to existing methods through clever combination of BFS-based layering and adjacency matrix compression

Comprehensive technical solution addressing real limitations: non-manifold edge handling, global structure awareness, and explicit geometric constraints (manifold topology, watertight detection, face normal consistency)
Thorough experimental evaluation on multiple datasets (gObjaverse, ShapeNet, 3D-FUTURE, Toy4K) with multiple baselines and both quantitative (5 metrics) and qualitative results
Strong geometric property guarantees with practical post-processing steps for watertight repair and support for small critical components, important for real applications
Clear presentation with well-designed algorithmic figures (Figs. 3-5), extensive appendix, and principled derivation of compression ratios using information-theoretic analysis
Measurable improvements: achieves 0.22 compression ratio (vs 0.26 for BPT), higher face number metric (1.321), and comparable or better geometry metrics across datasets
weaknesses: Incremental novelty: primarily combines existing techniques (BFS-based layering, matrix compression, decoder-only transformers) without introducing fundamentally new algorithmic or theoretical insights

Critical missing experimental comparisons: no inference speed/latency measurements despite practical importance; marked EdgeRunner comparison as unfair (different training data); missing recent auto-regressive baselines from 2024-2025

Scalability concerns inadequately addressed: maximum vocabulary constraint of 10,267 tokens unclear for larger meshes; dataset filtering criteria (Sec. 4.1) excludes unknown data portion; no analysis of generalization to filtered-out meshes or out-of-distribution cases
Non-manifold edge processing (Sec. 3.1, Appendix A) presents complex, ad-hoc partition rules without principled justification or ablation studies determining which rules are most important
Quantitative improvements are incremental: NC 0.830 vs 0.793 for BPT, CR 0.22 vs 0.26 (~8% gain), many metrics show 0.05-0.1 point improvements without statistical significance testing

Geometric property evaluation in Section 4.5 is primarily qualitative; claims of 'significantly improved geometric integrity' lack systematic quantitative analysis; watertight repair shown in single example (Fig. 9)

Progressive-balanced sampling strategy feels orthogonal to main contribution; straightforward interpolation between existing sampling methods without novel algorithmic insight; minimal ablation (only with/without, not different schedules)

Reproducibility: code and data promised as 'will be released' but not currently available; some implementation details relegated to appendix; dataset filtering criteria not fully explicit in main paper
Limited failure case analysis: Section 5 acknowledges constraints but lacks concrete examples; no evaluation on challenging inputs (high-genus surfaces, extremely irregular meshes, adversarial cases)

Non-standard evaluation metrics (NC, INCl) with limited justification; no perceptual user studies; compression ratio theoretical analysis assumes ideal 'degree ≈ 6' meshes, actual distributions vary significantly

strengths: Novel hierarchical vertex layering and sorting algorithm that provides canonical topological ordering while preserving manifold structure
Technically sound mesh tokenization approach with rigorous complexity analysis (O(K(E log E + V)))
Impressive compression efficiency: 0.22 compression ratio and 26.65 bits-per-face, state-of-the-art performance
Comprehensive experimental validation across multiple datasets (gObjaverse, 3D-FUTURE, ShapeNetV2, Toy3K) with quantitative metrics (CD, HD, NC, INCl) and qualitative comparisons
Well-designed practical contributions: online non-manifold processing, progressive-balanced resampling strategy, and part-aware generation capability
Clear presentation with effective algorithmic illustrations and detailed implementation details enabling reproducibility
Thorough ablation studies validating design choices (resampling strategy, non-manifold processing)
Addresses genuine practical limitation in auto-regressive mesh generation—failure to preserve geometric properties critical for gaming, VR, and CAD applications
weaknesses: Missing comparison with DeepMesh baseline (cited as omitted due to 'human feedback fine-tuning'), weakening baseline set
Some metric improvements are marginal (e.g., NC: 0.792 vs BPT 0.770 is ~2.8% improvement) without statistical significance testing or confidence intervals
Bits-per-face metric includes log(vocab_size) term, confounding cross-method comparison since different vocabulary sizes affect absolute scores
Hard constraints limit scalability: maximum vertices per layer (m=200), vocabulary size limit (10,267), predefined matrix size m
Window size parameters (W=8, W'=5) appear somewhat arbitrary; no systematic ablation or justification provided
Epoch threshold for resampling strategy transition (t/T = 0.5) lacks theoretical or empirical justification
Non-manifold processing rules in Appendix A appear heuristic; unclear if exhaustive for all edge cases
Limited evaluation of failure modes—failure case analysis (Appendix L) is brief and not well integrated into main results
No statistical significance testing or confidence intervals reported for any quantitative results
Missing analysis of computational efficiency during inference; no timing comparisons with baselines
7-bit quantization acknowledged to degrade fine geometric details; limited analysis of this trade-off
No evaluation across different mesh topologies (e.g., different genus); scalability to very high-resolution meshes not demonstrated
No mention of code availability or release plans, limiting reproducibility despite detailed descriptions
Limited user studies or perceptual quality assessment; all evaluation is computational metrics
Hyperparameter choices (e.g., specific filter settings) not fully justified throughout implementation details
